newsitem.title: FRANCE: Zaire rebel threatens attack on govt air base.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebel threatens attack on govt air base.

text.p: Zairean rebel leader Laurent Kabila threatened on Tuesday to attack the airport used by Zaire's air force to bomb three rebel-held towns in east Zaire on Monday.

"These are terrorist actions. And we are going to get ready to take the war precisely to the place from where the bombers took off," Kabila said in a brief interview broadcast on French LCI television.

In a marked escalation of the war between the Kinshasa army and Tutsi-led guerrillas, the Defence Ministry said Zairean planes bombed the towns of Bukavu, Shabunda and Walikale. A senior defence official said Goma, the biggest city in rebel hands, was next on the hit list.
Defence officials said the planes took off from Kisangani where President Mobutu Sese Seko has stationed newly acquired Russian-made jet fighters and helicopter gunships.
The air raids appeared designed as a psychological boost for Mobutu's bedraggled army which has lost a vast stretch of borderland to Tutsi-led rebels since October.
The medical charity Medecins sans Frontieres (MSF-Holland) said from Goma that at least nine people were killed and up to 37 wounded in the Bukavu bombing.
